title: 5.5.2 Sub-build: End and start again
description: A ball falls into a pit, the round ends after three seconds, and R starts it again. Build the smallest version of losing, before you put it into your table.

steps.title: Run it first
steps.instructions: The ball drops through the gap and keeps going. Nothing ends, and R does nothing.

steps.title: End the round
steps.instructions: Add a variable that says whether the round is still running. When the ball is below the canvas, set it to false. In `draw()`, only move and draw the game while it is true, and show "Game over" when it is false.
hints: `ball.y > height` is the usual pit test; `height` is the canvas height.
Do not delete the ball: the round ends, the game is still on screen.

steps.title: Start again with R
steps.instructions: On `kb.presses('r')`, put the ball back where it started, stop it moving, reset the score and set the round back to running.
hints: Put the restart in its own `if`, not inside the game-over branch, so it works from either state.
Set `ball.vel.x` and `ball.vel.y` to 0 as well as `ball.x` and `ball.y`, or it keeps its old speed.

requirements.title: A round can be over
requirements.description: A variable (lost / gameOver / playing) is set when the ball falls below the canvas, and the game checks it before moving or drawing. Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)

requirements.title: R puts the round back
requirements.description: R sets the ball back to its start and the game back to running. Help: 5.5.1 (Reading: The state of the game)
requirements.hint: if (kb.presses('r')) { ball.x = 200; ball.y = 60; ball.vel.x = 0; ball.vel.y = 0; playing = true; }

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a short moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: End and start again". The task: end the round when the ball falls below the canvas (a flag), keep the game on screen and show Game over, and let R put the ball back at its start with no velocity and set the round running again. This is a sub-build: a small isolated program whose only job is this one mechanic, so judge the mechanic itself and not style. Accept any variable names, helper functions, arrow functions, ternaries and semicolons. A line that only exists in a comment or a string does not count. moSHion facts: colliding(b) is 0 while apart and counts frames while touching, so an if on it alone is true every frame of a touch; a stored "last frame" value makes it true once. .life = n counts down one per frame and deletes the sprite at 0. A sprite with collider 'none' is passed through and has its gravity off. loadSound(name) in setup() (a built-in name such as 'coin', or a full path such as '/moshion/assets/coin.wav') and sound.play() where the event happens; a browser will not play sound before the student's first click or key. Write short, plain notes for a 14-year-old, name the student's own line when something is missing, and never write corrected code.

rubric.title: The round ends
rubric.description: A flag is set when the ball leaves the bottom of the canvas, and the game stops moving or scoring when it is set.

rubric.title: R restarts
rubric.description: R resets the ball's position and velocity and sets the round back to running; the score is reset too.
